explanation: So the expression simplifies to $\cos^2\theta$, and the power is $n = 2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test it with real numbers
steps: And cos 30° ≈ 0.866, so cos² 30° ≈ 0.75. They match, so the power is 2, not 1.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think of a full pie
steps: The identity says sin² and cos² are two slices that together make one whole pie.
Take the sin² slice away from the whole pie and what is left is exactly the cos² slice.
